title: Weak delocalization of a resolution at a minimal prime over the singular ideal
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A$ an $R$-algebra of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras and $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime ideal, with $\mathfrak h_A=\sqrt{H_{A/R}\Lambda}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution] ($H_{A/R}$ the singular ideal [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]). Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ the localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $A_{\mathfrak p}=A\otimes_RR_{\mathfrak p}$ (of finite presentation over $R_{\mathfrak p}$, with the induced map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$). Assume that $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $\mathfrak h_A$ and that $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\supset\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ can be resolved [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]. Then there is a factorization $A\xrightarrow{\beta}C\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Lambda$ of $\alpha$ by homomorphisms of $R$-algebras with $C$ of finite presentation over $R$ such that $H_{C/R}\Lambda\not\subset\mathfrak q$, where $H_{C/R}\Lambda$ is the ideal of $\Lambda$ generated by $\gamma(H_{C/R})$ (equivalently $\mathfrak h_C=\sqrt{H_{C/R}\Lambda}\not\subset\mathfrak q$).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak, line 2148), Section 07F6 (section-local); reference Swan, Lemma 12.2, or Popescu GND, Lemma 2

proof.text: (The localized resolution has unit singular ideal.) Let $A_{\mathfrak p}\xrightarrow{\beta_1}C_1\xrightarrow{\gamma_1}\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ be a resolution of $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\supset\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]: $C_1$ is an $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra of finite presentation, $\gamma_1\beta_1$ is the map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ induced by $\alpha$, and $\mathfrak h_{C_1}=\sqrt{H_{C_1/R_{\mathfrak p}}\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}}\not\subset\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. The ring $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], so the ideal $\mathfrak h_{C_1}$, not contained in the maximal ideal, is $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$; then $1\in\sqrt{H_{C_1/R_{\mathfrak p}}\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}}$, i.e. $1=1^k\in H_{C_1/R_{\mathfrak p}}\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, so $H_{C_1/R_{\mathfrak p}}\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$. (Stacks attributes this to the minimality of $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak h_A$; the argument above shows that only the locality of $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is needed, and the minimality hypothesis is not used anywhere in the proof.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2163-2167

proof.text: (Reduction to a smooth $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra.) By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-final-solve] (Stacks 07EU) applied to $R_{\mathfrak p}\to C_1\xrightarrow{\gamma_1}\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ ($C_1$ of finite presentation over $R_{\mathfrak p}$, $H_{C_1/R_{\mathfrak p}}\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ by Step 1) there are a smooth $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra $C_2$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra maps $C_1\xrightarrow{\delta}C_2\xrightarrow{\gamma_2}\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ with $\gamma_2\delta=\gamma_1$. Hence $A_{\mathfrak p}\xrightarrow{\delta\beta_1}C_2\xrightarrow{\gamma_2}\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ factors the map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ induced by $\alpha$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2168-2169

proof.text: (Reduction to a standard smooth $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra.) By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-retract-standard-smooth] (Stacks 07CH) applied to the smooth $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra $C_2$ there are a standard smooth $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra $D$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] and $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra maps $\iota:C_2\to D$, $\rho:D\to C_2$ with $\rho\iota=\mathrm{id}_{C_2}$. Put $\beta_D=\iota\delta\beta_1:A_{\mathfrak p}\to D$ and $\gamma_D=\gamma_2\rho:D\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$; then $\gamma_D\beta_D=\gamma_2\rho\iota\delta\beta_1=\gamma_2\delta\beta_1=\gamma_1\beta_1$ is the map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ induced by $\alpha$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2170-2171

proof.text: (Generators of $A$ and their images.) Fix a presentation $A\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_t)$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], let $\bar x_i\in A$ be the class of $x_i$ and $\lambda_i=\alpha(\bar x_i)\in\Lambda$, $i=1,\dots,n$. Since $\alpha$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras, $g_j(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)=\alpha(g_j(\bar x_1,\dots,\bar x_n))=\alpha(0)=0$ in $\Lambda$ for $j=1,\dots,t$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $a_i=\beta_D(\bar x_i\otimes1)\in D$. The map $A_{\mathfrak p}=A\otimes_RR_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ induced by $\alpha$ sends $\bar x_i\otimes1$ to $\lambda_i/1$, so $\gamma_D(a_i)=\lambda_i/1$ by Step 3.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2172-2173

proof.text: (A standard smooth presentation of $D$ containing the generators of $A$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-include-generators] (Stacks 07EY) applied to the standard smooth $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra $D$ and $a_1,\dots,a_n$ there are $m\ge0$, $n\le c\le n+m$, $f_1,\dots,f_c\in P':=R_{\mathfrak p}[x_1,\dots,x_{n+m}]$ and an isomorphism of $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebras $P'/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\cong D$ sending the class of $x_i$ to $a_i$ ($i\le n$), such that $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j=1,\dots,c}$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] is invertible in $D$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]. We identify $D=P'/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$; then $\beta_D$ sends $\bar x_i\otimes1$ to the class of $x_i$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2174-2178

proof.text: ($P'$ is the localization of $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+m}]$ at $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$.) $R_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}R$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $\varphi:P\to P'$ apply $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ to the coefficients. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] $P'\cong R_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RP$ compatibly with $\varphi$ ($p\mapsto1\otimes p$), and by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] (with $D=P$ and $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ the localization at $S$) $P\to P\otimes_RR_{\mathfrak p}$ is a localization of $P$ at the image of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Hence: (a) every element of $P'$ is $u^{-1}\varphi(p)$ with $p\in P$, $u\in S$, and finitely many elements have a common denominator (the product of the denominators); (b) $\varphi(p)=\varphi(q)$ implies $vp=vq$ for some $v\in S$; (c) every $u\in S$ is a unit in $P'$. Moreover (d) $\varphi$ commutes with each $\partial/\partial x_i$ (both are computed coefficientwise by the monomial formula [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]) and hence with Jacobian determinants.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2179-2181 ('after clearing denominators')

proof.text: (Clearing the denominators of the $f_j$.) By Step 6(a) write $f_j=u_j^{-1}\varphi(p_j)$ with $p_j\in P$, $u_j\in S$. Since $u_j$ is a unit of $P'$ (Step 6(c)), replacing $f_j$ by $u_jf_j=\varphi(p_j)$ changes neither the ideal $(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ nor the classes of the $x_i$, hence neither $D$ nor $\beta_D,\gamma_D$, and it multiplies $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j\le c}$ by the unit $u_1\cdots u_c$ ($\partial/\partial x_i$ is $R_{\mathfrak p}$-linear and the determinant is linear in each row [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]), so it stays invertible in $D$. Hence we may assume $f_j=\varphi(f_j^0)$ with $f_j^0\in P$; we write $f_j$ for $f_j^0\in P$ from now on, and $\Delta=\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j=1,\dots,c}\in P$, so that $\varphi(\Delta)$ is the Jacobian determinant of the $\varphi(f_j)$ (Step 6(d)) and is invertible in $D=P'/(\varphi(f_1),\dots,\varphi(f_c))$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2179-2181

proof.text: (The element $s_0$.) Since $\varphi(\Delta)$ is invertible in $D$ there are $a'_0,\dots,a'_c\in P'$ with $1=a'_0\varphi(\Delta)+\sum_{j=1}^ca'_j\varphi(f_j)$. By Step 6(a) write $a'_j=u^{-1}\varphi(a''_j)$ ($j=0,\dots,c$) with $a''_j\in P$ and one $u\in S$; multiplying by $u$ gives $\varphi(u)=\varphi(a''_0\Delta+\sum_ja''_jf_j)$, so by Step 6(b) [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] $v(u-a''_0\Delta-\sum_ja''_jf_j)=0$ in $P$ for some $v\in S$. With $s_0=vu\in S$ and $h=va''_0\in P$: $s_0-h\Delta=\sum_jva''_jf_j\in(f_1,\dots,f_c)P$. (This is what Stacks means by 'it becomes invertible after inverting some $s_0\in R$, $s_0\notin\mathfrak p$'.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2182-2185

proof.text: (The elements $s_1,\dots,s_t$.) The image of $\varphi(g_j)$ ($g_j\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\subset P$) in $D$ is $g_j$ evaluated at the classes of $x_1,\dots,x_n$, which is $\beta_D(g_j(\bar x_1,\dots,\bar x_n)\otimes1)=\beta_D(0)=0$ by Steps 4 and 5 ($\beta_D$ is an $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra map sending $\bar x_i\otimes1$ to the class of $x_i$) [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. So $\varphi(g_j)=\sum_kh_k\varphi(f_k)$ with $h_k\in P'$; writing $h_k=u^{-1}\varphi(h'_k)$ (Step 6(a)) gives $\varphi(ug_j)=\varphi(\sum_kh'_kf_k)$, so $v(ug_j-\sum_kh'_kf_k)=0$ for some $v\in S$ (Step 6(b) [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]). With $s_j=vu\in S$: $s_jg_j\in(f_1,\dots,f_c)P$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2186-2188

proof.text: (The elements $\lambda_{n+1},\dots,\lambda_{n+m+1}$.) For $i=1,\dots,m$ write $\gamma_D(\text{class of }x_{n+i})=\mu_i/u_i$ with $\mu_i\in\Lambda$, $u_i\in\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Put $\lambda_{n+m+1}=u_1\cdots u_m$ ($=1$ if $m=0$), which is not in $\mathfrak q$ as $\mathfrak q$ is prime, and $\lambda_{n+i}=\mu_i\prod_{k\ne i}u_k$; then $\gamma_D(\text{class of }x_{n+i})=\lambda_{n+i}/\lambda_{n+m+1}$ in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ for $i=1,\dots,m$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2193-2195

proof.text: (Homogenization and the element $\lambda_0$.) For $j=1,\dots,c$ write $f_j=\sum_{e\in\mathbf N^m}a_{j,e}x_{n+1}^{e_1}\cdots x_{n+m}^{e_m}$ with $a_{j,e}\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, let $d_j$ be the total degree of $f_j$ in $x_{n+1},\dots,x_{n+m}$ (the maximum of $|e|=e_1+\dots+e_m$ over $a_{j,e}\ne0$; $0$ if $f_j=0$) and $F_j=\sum_ea_{j,e}X_{n+1}^{e_1}\cdots X_{n+m}^{e_m}X_{n+m+1}^{d_j-|e|}\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n,X_{n+1},\dots,X_{n+m+1}]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], so $f_j=F_j(x_1,\dots,x_{n+m},1)$. The $R$-algebra maps $P\xrightarrow{\varphi}P'\to D\xrightarrow{\gamma_D}\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ and the evaluation $P\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ at $(\lambda_1/1,\dots,\lambda_n/1,\lambda_{n+1}/\lambda_{n+m+1},\dots,\lambda_{n+m}/\lambda_{n+m+1})$ agree on every $x_i$ (Steps 4, 5, 10), hence are equal; since $\varphi(f_j)$ maps to $0$ in $D$, $f_j(\lambda_1/1,\dots,\lambda_{n+m}/\lambda_{n+m+1})=0$ in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$. Multiplying by $(\lambda_{n+m+1}/1)^{d_j}$ term by term, $a_{j,e}(\lambda)\prod_k(\lambda_{n+k}/\lambda_{n+m+1})^{e_k}\cdot\lambda_{n+m+1}^{d_j}=a_{j,e}(\lambda)\prod_k\lambda_{n+k}^{e_k}\lambda_{n+m+1}^{d_j-|e|}$, gives $F_j(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_{n+m+1})/1=0$ in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$. So there is $v_j\in\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $v_jF_j(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_{n+m+1})=0$ in $\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; put $\lambda_0=v_1\cdots v_c\notin\mathfrak q$ ($\mathfrak q$ prime), so $\lambda_0F_j(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_{n+m+1})=0$ for all $j$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2189-2211

proof.text: (The factorization.) Let $B=R[x_0,x_1,\dots,x_n,X_{n+1},\dots,X_{n+m+1}]/(g_1,\dots,g_t,x_0F_1,\dots,x_0F_c)$, an $R$-algebra of finite presentation ($n+m+2$ variables, $t+c$ relations) [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. The $R$-algebra map $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to B$, $x_i\mapsto$ class of $x_i$, kills each $g_j$, so it induces $\beta:A\to B$, $\bar x_i\mapsto$ class of $x_i$. The evaluation $R[x_0,\dots,X_{n+m+1}]\to\Lambda$, $x_0\mapsto\lambda_0$, $x_i\mapsto\lambda_i$, $X_{n+k}\mapsto\lambda_{n+k}$, kills $g_j$ (Step 4) and $x_0F_j$ (Step 11) [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], so it induces $\gamma:B\to\Lambda$. Then $\gamma\beta(\bar x_i)=\lambda_i=\alpha(\bar x_i)$ for all $i$, and since the $\bar x_i$ generate $A$ as an $R$-algebra, $\gamma\beta=\alpha$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2212-2218

proof.text: ($B_b$ is smooth.) Let $b\in B$ be the class of $x_0X_{n+m+1}s_0s_1\cdots s_t$. The data $R$, $n,m,c,t$ ($c\le n+m$ by Step 5), $f_1,\dots,f_c\in P$ (Step 7), $g_1,\dots,g_t$, $s_0,\dots,s_t$ satisfy hypothesis (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-delocalize-weak-localization-smooth] with $h$ from Step 8 and hypothesis (ii) by Step 9; the $F_j$ of Step 11 are the polynomials of that node with $d_j$ the total degree, and $B$, $b$ are the algebra and the element there. Hence $B_b$ is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2219-2225

proof.text:
(Conclusion.) By Step 13 and the definition of the singular ideal [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], $b$ lies in the set $G$ of elements $g\in B$ with $B_g$ smooth over $R$, hence $b\in H_{B/R}=\sqrt{(G)}$. Its image $\gamma(b)=\lambda_0\lambda_{n+m+1}\sigma(s_0)\sigma(s_1)\cdots\sigma(s_t)$ ($\sigma:R	o\Lambda$ the structure map) is not in $\mathfrak q$: $\lambda_0
otin\mathfrak q$ (Step 11), $\lambda_{n+m+1}
otin\mathfrak q$ (Step 10), and $s_j\in S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ with $\mathfrak p=\sigma^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ gives $\sigma(s_j)
otin\mathfrak q$; as $\mathfrak q$ is prime the product is not in $\mathfrak q$. Thus $H_{B/R}\Lambda
ot\subset\mathfrak q$, and $C=B$ with $ eta,\gamma$ of Step 12 is the required factorization.

split_report.summary: Proof written in 14 steps following the Stacks proof of 07F9 line by line, on the model of the split of 07F4 (lem-weil-pbc-popescu-delocalize-base), whose localization nodes are reused. Steps: the localized resolution has unit singular ideal (Lambda_q local; the minimality of q over h_A, which Stacks invokes here, is not needed and not used anywhere); reduction to C smooth over R_p by 07EU (lem-weil-pbc-popescu-final-solve), to C standard smooth by 07CH (lem-weil-pbc-smooth-retract-standard-smooth, a retraction, not a replacement: the factorization is rerouted through D and the retraction); presentation of A and lambda_i; standard smooth presentation containing the generators (07EY); P' = localization of P at S = R minus p (polynomial-scalar-extension, localization-base-change leaves); clearing denominators of the f_j, the relation s_0 - h Delta in (f), the s_j with s_j g_j in (f) (Stacks one sentence each, written out); common denominator lambda_{n+m+1}; homogenization F_j and lambda_0 (the identity written monomialwise); B, beta, gamma; B_b smooth (one new node: the isomorphism B_b = R_s[x_0^{+-1}, X_{n+m+1}^{+-1}, x, y]/(f) needs the change of variables y_i = X_{n+i}/X_{n+m+1}, which Stacks's displayed formula leaves implicit, and then a standard smooth presentation); conclusion b in H_{B/R} from the definition. Statement unchanged in content; the finite presentation notion is now cited (def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra added to stmt_deps).

reviewed.note: 14 steps following Stacks 07F9: the localized resolution has unit singular ideal (Lambda_q local; the minimality hypothesis is not used, as the worker notes); reduction to a smooth then standard smooth R_p-algebra (07EU, 07CH nodes); a standard smooth presentation containing the generators of A (07EY node); P' as the localization of P, clearing denominators, the elements s_0, s_j, the lambda's; homogenization; the algebra B and the factorization; B_b smooth as a new unsplit node (the implicit change of variables x_{n+i} -> X_{n+i}/X_{n+m+1} written into its statement); conclusion. Statement gained the finitely-presented citation.
